Hi Leighann,

Thank you for passing along this feedback.

Our Engineering team recently deployed an update aimed at improving performance, which may have resolved this behavior. Since the export is functioning as expected in Chrome, the issue in Microsoft Edge could likely be temporary or related to cached data.

To help us narrow this down, could you please ask the Power User to try the following steps?

  1. Browser Cache & Cookies: Clear cache and cookies in Microsoft Edge, or test the export using an InPrivate / Incognito window.

  2. Re-test the Export: Verify if data can now be exported in Edge as well.

If the issue persists after trying these steps, please let us know and provide:

  • The specific report names or URLs that are failing to export.

  • Any screenshots of error messages or unexpected behavior in Edge.

We appreciate your help in verifying this so we can ensure everything is working seamlessly across all supported browsers!

Best regards,
Viraj Kansara
Retail Customer Support

CLIENT: Ahold Delhaize USA / ADUSA (Client ID 441)

I reproduced this in production on 14 August 2026 on Unusual Incidents Details, /adusa/nettrack/AdHoc/ReportViewer.aspx. There were nine updates between 12:04 and 12:20.

The saved default range on the report is 6/17/2019 to 6/17/2020. Setting it to 6/1/2026 and 8/14/2026 yielded all four possible outcomes:
Range held at 2026, results 2019 and 2020. Three times.
Range reverted to 2019 and 2020, results 2019 and 2020. Three times.
Range reverted to 2019 and 2020, results 2026. Once.
Range held at 2026, results 2026. Once.

The date shown on screen and the data returned are independent of each other. There is no error at any point.

The data is present. 2026 records were returned on two runs, so this is not missing data and not a pre migration source.

This matches symptom B on ENG-5649, recorded there as not yet isolated separately. The difference from the Guess analysis on that ticket is that here rs.aspx reaches the response server and returns 200, so the designer backend is not dead on this tenant.

Cookies during the test: pCohesion=50012-441, izscResponseServer=/adusa/nettrack/AdHoc/rs.aspx, ntWEBCFG has PLT=0 and PLTFRMID=441. ENG-5649 records PLT=1 on Guess. It is worth confirming whether any code path selects the connection using PLT rather than pCohesion.

Cache, cookies, and InPrivate were ruled out before this test.

Hi @leighann.stubbs@adusa.com

We now have specific report names to work from, which is what we were missing before. Jim confirmed that PBI - Incident Export 2026 Q3 fails when exporting to CSV and succeeds when exporting to XLS, and that PBI - Current Location Listing fails on both. He also confirmed this morning that both are still failing today. That difference between formats, and between one report and another, gives us something concrete to trace.

Two things that would help us match your case to his:

When you click Export to Excel and nothing happens, is that on one specific report or on every report you try?

Does the same report export if you choose CSV instead of Excel?

Separately, the Central Division count in Interview Data with Source was confirmed correct this morning by both you and Jim, so that piece is closed on our side. The export failure you described stays open here until you tell us it works.

Thanks

","created":"2026-08-19T18:14:14.245-0400","updated":"2026-08-19T18:14:14.245-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"jsdPublic":true},{"id":"3300385","author":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"body":"

RCS-28021 and RCS-28413 are being treated as one item in places and they are two.

RCS-28413 is the count discrepancy, 66 cases for Central against an expected 268 as of 27 July 2026 in Interview Data with Source (AP REPORTS FOOD LION). Leigh Ann confirmed at 10:26 today and Jim at 14:44 that the report is returning correctly. Ready to close.

RCS-28021 is the export failing to produce a file. Jim confirmed at 11:34 today that it is still happening, with screenshots of PBI - Merchandise Export Q3-2026 and PBI - Current Location Listing, and he also hit several 502s while navigating Izenda.

Named reports from Jim on 18 August, which answers the request for one report by name: PBI - Incident Export 2026 Q3 (Jim Cosseboom Test), CSV fails and XLS succeeds, and the scheduled CSV delivered by email did work. PBI - Current Location Listing (Jim Cosseboom Test), fails on both CSV and XLS.

The scheduled delivery working while the on demand export fails points at the export path rather than at the report definition or the underlying data.

The Izenda app service and load balancing work with Jack was described in this morning's review as being at a should be working state in test. Confirming whether that reaches this symptom tells us whether to wait for it or trace separately.

Export Instruction in PROD:

. Big Reports PDF export:
. It can cause timeout
. Recommended to export to Excel or DOC and convert to PDF by users if required
. Keep estimate time of export for those big reports if possible
. If any report takes longer than 3 minutes for any type of export, starting with CSV, pass it to ApprissRetail, we will handle it individually
